title: Maximum Square Area by Removing Fences From a Field
summary: Given a rectangular field with corners at (1, 1) and (m, n), containing horizontal and vertical fences defined by arrays hFences and vFences, determine the maximum area of a square field that can be formed by removing some fences.
statement: Given a rectangular field with corners at (1, 1) and (m, n), containing horizontal and vertical fences defined by arrays hFences and vFences, determine the maximum area of a square field that can be formed by removing some fences. If no square field can be formed, return -1. The field is surrounded by two horizontal and two vertical fences that cannot be removed. The result should be modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: m and n are at least three; interior fence positions are unique and strictly inside their dimension.
Boundary fences at positions one and m or n cannot be removed.
Choose equal horizontal and vertical coordinate gaps; return the largest square area modulo 1,000,000,007, or -1.
hints: Removing intermediate fences exposes every distance between two retained coordinate lines.
Enumerate all pairwise horizontal and vertical gaps, intersect the sets, and select the largest common gap.
Add immutable boundaries, build distance sets from every pair, take max intersection, square modulo M.
Any square is bounded by two lines in each direction with one common gap, and every shared gap can be realized by removing intervening fences.
editorial: Any square is bounded by two lines in each direction with one common gap, and every shared gap can be realized by removing intervening fences.

tests.explanation: Both dimensions can expose a gap of two, producing square area four.
The available horizontal and vertical coordinate gaps have no common value, so no square is possible.
